module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's Open Problem 24

References:
- [Green, Ben. "100 open problems." (2024).](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.24)
- [Aa19] Aaronson, James. "Maximising the number of solutions to a linear equation in a set of integers."
  Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society 51.4 (2019): 577-594.
- [HaL28] Hardy, G. H., and J. E. Littlewood. "Notes on the theory of series (VIII): an inequality."
  Journal of the London Mathematical Society 1.2 (1928): 105-110.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Green24

/--
The maximum number of $\lbrace 0,1,3 \rbrace$ affine translates that a set of size $n$ can
contain.
-/
noncomputable def max013AffineTranslates (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup { k |
    ∃ A : Finset ℤ,
      A.card = n ∧
      -- Iterate over (x,y) = (a, a + d) in A × A (x ≠ y), and check if a + 3d = x + 3(y - x) ∈ A
      k = ((A ×ˢ A).filter (fun (x, y) ↦ x ≠ y ∧ x + 3 * (y - x) ∈ A)).card
  }

/--
If $A$ is a set of $n$ integers, what is the maximum number of affine translates of the set
$\lbrace 0,1,3 \rbrace$ that $A$ can contain?

Conjectured in [Aa19] p.579: $\left(\frac{1}{3} + o(1)\right) n^2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem green_24 : ∀ n, max013AffineTranslates n = (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℕ) n := by
  sorry

/-  A collection of associated bounds and conjectured values. -/

namespace variants


/-- From [Aa19] p.577: the trivial upper bound is $n^2$ (non asymptotic). -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem upper_trivial {n : ℕ} : max013AffineTranslates n ≤ n ^ 2 := by
  apply csSup_le
  · exact ⟨_, ⟨(Finset.range n).image Int.ofNat, by
      rw [Finset.card_image_of_injective _ Int.ofNat_injective, Finset.card_range], rfl⟩⟩
  · rintro k ⟨A, hA, rfl⟩
    apply le_trans (Finset.card_filter_le _ _)
    rw [Finset.card_product, hA, pow_two]

/-- The asymptotic constant $\gamma$ defined in [Aa19] p.579. -/
noncomputable def gamma : ℝ :=
  limsup (fun n : ℕ => (max013AffineTranslates n : ℝ) / ((n : ℝ)^2)) atTop

/-- Asymptotic upper bound (1.2) in [Aa19]. Named after Hardy and Littlewood [HaL28]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem upper_HL : gamma ≤ 3/4 := by
  sorry

/-- Asymptotic lower bound (1.2) in [Aa19]. Named after Hardy and Littlewood [HaL28]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem lower_HL : gamma ≥ 1/12 := by
  sorry

/-- Conjecture p.579 in [Aa19]: $\left(\frac{1}{3} + o(1)\right) n^2$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5 11]
theorem conjecture : gamma = 1/3 := by
  sorry

end variants

end Green24

findings.description: The [HaL28] reference gives the journal volume/issue as “1.2”. The article appeared in first-series volume 3, issue 2, not volume 1. This is only a bibliographic error; the mathematical statements are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: The publisher-supplied Crossref record for “Notes on the Theory of Series (VIII): An Inequality”, DOI 10.1112/jlms/s1-3.2.105, records volume “s1-3”, issue “2”, pages 105–110, April 1928: https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1112/jlms/s1-3.2.105 .
findings.suggested_fix: Change the reference to “Journal of the London Mathematical Society, s1-3(2) (1928), 105–110.”

reformulations.difference: Aaronson takes the limsup of T(S)/|S|² over finite integer sets as their cardinality tends to infinity, counting all ordered solutions to x + 2y = 3z. Lean instead takes the limsup over cardinalities of the maximum number of nondegenerate affine copies.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every finite A, the ordered equation solutions are in bijection with pairs (a,b) in A² satisfying a + 3(b−a) ∈ A. Exactly |A| are diagonal. Thus T(A) equals the Lean copy count plus |A|, and the maximum equation count at size n equals max013AffineTranslates n + n. The normalized difference is 1/n, which tends to zero. Maximizing separately at each cardinality preserves the source’s limsup because the maxima are attained. In /workspace/review/equivalence.lean I proved equality between the file’s γ and the source’s all-finite-sets limsup, using the filter comap Finset.card atTop, and proved the corresponding conjecture equivalence. The proof has no sorry dependency.

reformulations.difference: The theorem asserts γ = 1/3, matching Aaronson directly, while Green and the docstring also express the conjecture as max013AffineTranslates n = (1/3 + o(1))n², a full asymptotic rather than merely a limsup value.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The interval {0,…,n−1} contains 2·Σ_{d=1}^{⌊(n−1)/3⌋}(n−3d) = n²/3 − n + O(1) nondegenerate copies, counting both signs of the dilation. Consequently the normalized extremal count has liminf at least 1/3. Its limsup equals 1/3 if and only if the normalized count converges to 1/3. Thus the limsup formulation does not weaken Green’s asymptotic conjecture.

sources_consulted: Ben Green, “100 open problems”, Problem 24 and comments; the downloaded version records its latest update as December 2025: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.24

James Aaronson, “Maximising the number of solutions to a linear equation in a set of integers”, arXiv:1801.07135v4, Introduction: definition of T(S), trivial upper bound, lower-bound construction, definition of γ, equation (1.2), and the conjecture for γ_{1,2,-3}. LaTeX source: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1801.07135 ; abstract and version history: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.07135 .

Crossref title-search metadata for Aaronson’s article, DOI 10.1112/blms.12253: https://api.crossref.org/works?query.title=Maximising%20the%20number%20of%20solutions%20to%20a%20linear%20equation%20in%20a%20set%20of%20integers&rows=3

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization found. Checked all two definitions and five theorems. Lean experiments established nonemptiness and boundedness of the set in sSup, attainment of the maximum, values 0 at n = 0, 1, 2, a positive value at n = 3, boundedness of the normalized sequence, and uniqueness of the affine-copy parametrization. The answer slot is constrained, and the recorded open/solved statuses agree with the consulted sources. Scratch proofs are in /workspace/review/sanity.lean and /workspace/review/equivalence.lean. The original Hardy–Littlewood full text could not be retrieved from Wiley; both bounds used by this file were verified explicitly in Aaronson’s source.
